title: Map-time on_ui_press reads pre-Cancel selection: same-frame ESC + popover/QoS click logs commands the old handle_input never produced
detail: The B2 fix advanced placing (placing_eff) and the latch (Press_Anchor) but not the selection the UI hooks read. Same-frame ESC+demolish-button click: old deselected first (popover_click false, no command); new logs the demolish, then deselects. Same for QoS row clicks (Set_Lane). Mouse-path delta = blocker. Existed at r1 (2f5027a mouse.odin:140), r1 missed it.
recommended_fix: When mouse_map emits an ESC Cancel, also clear inp.sel_pipe/sel_node at map time (extend the placing_eff pattern), so on_ui_press evaluates the post-cancel state, exactly mirroring the old sequential order.

title: input_parity_reject's selection assert is vacuous — sel_node and sel_pipe are mutually exclusive, so the && condition can never fire
evidence:
parity.odin:807-808: `case "input_parity_reject":
		if r, ok := find(runs, devs, .Mouse); ok && r.sel_node != -1 && r.sel_pipe != -1 {` with message `a rejected draw must not change the selection`. exec.odin click_select: `inp.sel_node = i64(id)
			inp.sel_pipe = -1` and the pipe branch `inp.sel_pipe = i64(pid)
			inp.sel_node = -1` — every selection path keeps one of the two at -1.
detail: Selection is mutually exclusive by construction (click_select, right_click_select, Cancel, demolish all clear the twin), so both fields != -1 simultaneously is unreachable and this pin can never fail. A regression that selects a pipe OR node after the rejected draw passes silently.
recommended_fix: Change the condition to `r.sel_node != -1 || r.sel_pipe != -1` so a spurious post-reject selection actually fails the scenario.

title: mouse_map's fixed moves[2] buffer silently drops the 3rd+ Mouse_Move of a frame
detail: The cap matches the live poller (one Mouse_Move/frame) but scripted harness frames can exceed it; excess moves vanish silently. Command outcomes are unaffected (the release re-snaps), but intermediate drag/placement preview state can diverge from the script without any failure.
recommended_fix: Surface the overflow (a debug assert/fail in the harness path) or document the per-frame move cap as part of the Device_Event frame contract.

title: Retired 'Emphasis' terminology survives in new 5.4 code, and the relocation comment cites a self-referential rename
detail: The #55 rename (Cmd_Set_Emphasis -> Cmd_Set_Weights) is adopted for the types but the new parity test's failure output still prints 'Emphasis', and the main.odin comment describes the rename as Cmd_Set_Weights -> Cmd_Set_Weights, which documents nothing and confuses future readers.
recommended_fix: Print `Weights{%d,%v}@%d` in cmd_string, reword the parity.odin:701 comment to Set_Weights, and fix main.odin to read `the #55 terminology rename (Cmd_Set_Emphasis -> Cmd_Set_Weights)`.
